title: Hang a coat rack on the wall by its two keyhole slots
instruction: Hang the coat rack on the wall.
context: Keyhole slots are how coat racks, floating shelves, key holders and towel rails go up, and everyone who has hung one knows the fumbling: the slots are behind the piece, so both have to find their screw at once without being seen, by feel. The rack is lifted over the two screw heads, pushed flat to the wall so the heads enter the slots, and lowered until the shanks sit in the slots' throats and it hangs. The ability tested is a blind two-point alignment with a push-then-drop motion, with the piece held level throughout.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers at the near edge of a table, bases 61 cm apart. Positions are (x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the left of their midpoint) in cm; heights are above the table. (1) A section of wall: 18 mm plywood painted off-white, 60 cm wide and 20 cm tall, standing upright across the table and fixed to it, its face at x = 38, from y = -30 to +30. (2) Two No. 8 zinc-plated pan-head screws driven into the wall at y = +15 and -15, 10 cm above the table, their heads left 7.5 mm proud (4 mm shank; 8 mm head, 2.5 mm thick, domed to 5 mm at its top). (3) A pencil tick on the wall at each end of where the rack's top edge goes: y = +23 and -23, 11.3 cm above the table. (4) The coat rack, loose, 0.70 kg: a 40 x 8 x 2.5 cm dark-stained oak rail with three cast aluminium hooks screwed to its face at y = 0 and +-16 (30 x 40 mm base plate, a 50 mm arm standing out, 16 mm wide, turned up 45 mm at its end), and two keyhole slots routed into its back at y = +-15: a 14 mm square entry pocket 8 mm deep with its centre 30 mm below the top edge, a 12 mm channel running up from it behind a 2.5 mm lip that leaves a 6 mm throat; the entry's bottom edge and the lips' bottom edges are eased 2 mm. It stands upright on its bottom edge in front of the wall, hooks toward the robot, centred on y = 0, with its back 5 cm from the wall and its hooks' tips at x = 26. Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Final state, from a photo in front, a spirit level and a tug. Hanging on a keyhole: the screw's shank is in the slot's throat with the rack's weight on the screw (in the sim: the shank's centre within 1.5 mm of the throat's centre line and within 1.5 mm of where the rack comes to rest on the screw, behind the lip). A head sitting in the entry pocket only, or the rack held part way down the throats, does not count: let go, it would fall. Hung: hanging on both keyholes, the rack's lowest point at least 1 cm above the table, every corner of its back within 4 mm of the wall, its top edge within 5 mm of the pencilled height, and its long edge within 1 degree of level. Released: both grippers' centre points (between the finger pads) at least 3 cm from the rack. 1.0: hung, both grippers released, the rack still, held for 2 s; this ends the run. Hung at the end of the run with a gripper still touching also scores 1.0, checked by opening the grippers after the run: the rack must stay hanging. 0.5: hanging on one keyhole only (the other end dropped or never caught). 0: anything else, including the rack on the table, held in the air, leaning on the wall, or with the heads in the entries only.
run_limit: 3,200 control steps at 20 Hz (160 seconds of simulation time); full success ends the run early.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the rack back on its mark, upright, hooks toward the robot.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz, 20 Hz control, objects at real size and mass. The rack is one rigid body with a convex collider per part, the keyhole slots left open between the pieces of its back; the screws are fixed 12-sided shanks with domed heads; the wall a fixed box. Friction estimated: rack 0.45/0.40, screws 0.35/0.30, pads 0.5. Simplified: square entry pockets, not round; uniform density puts the centre of mass 7 mm behind the real rack's (both stand upright); the wall section is short.
